body:
In Texas, painting the outside of a typical 2,000 sq ft home costs about **$2,800 to $7,500** in 2026, or $1.40 to $3.75 per square foot of living area. That is our estimate, built from national prices and what painters in Texas actually earn: a median of $21.86 an hour, 8% below the national median of $23.75.

| | Texas | National |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per sq ft of home | $1.40 to $3.75 | $1.50 to $4.00 |
| 2,000 sq ft home | $2,800 to $7,500 | $3,000 to $8,000 |
| Painter median wage | $21.86 an hour | $23.75 an hour |

## Texas exterior painting cost by home size

| Home size (living area) | Typical cost in Texas |
| --- | --- |
| 1,500 sq ft | $2,100 to $5,625 |
| 2,000 sq ft | $2,800 to $7,500 |
| 2,500 sq ft | $3,500 to $9,375 |
| 3,000 sq ft | $4,200 to $11,250 |

These are typical ranges for a full repaint with normal prep. A small, simple house with sound paint lands near the low end. Two stories, heavy scraping, wood repairs or premium paint push you toward the top. Enter your own home size and any quote you have in the calculator above.

## Prices in Texas's largest metro areas

Painter wages are not the same across the state, so neither are prices. Here is the same 2,000 sq ft house in Texas's major metro areas:

| Metro area | Painter median wage | 2,000 sq ft home |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Houston-Pasadena-The Woodlands | $22.18 | $2,841 to $7,577 |
| Dallas-Fort Worth-Arlington | $21.90 | $2,813 to $7,501 |
| Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos | $22.38 | $2,862 to $7,631 |
| San Antonio-New Braunfels | $20.88 | $2,710 to $7,227 |

The gap between Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos and San Antonio-New Braunfels is $1.50 an hour in wages, which works out to roughly $152 to $404 on this one job. Small towns and rural areas usually sit closer to the lower metro numbers.

## What affects the price in Texas

**Siding.** Brick is the most common wall material on new Texas-area homes. In the West South Central region, which includes Texas, 54% of new single-family homes started in 2025 had brick or brick veneer walls, according to NAHB. Brick is usually left unpainted, so on many Texas houses the paint job is mostly trim, soffits, fascia, doors and any wood or fiber cement siding. That can put a full-brick house well under the per-square-foot range, so ask for a quote based on what will actually be painted.

**Weather and timing.** Cold is rarely the problem here; rain and humidity are. Sherwin-Williams says the first 48 hours after painting are the critical drying window, and paint needs dry weather to cure, so a good painter watches the forecast and works around storms. Spring and fall are the easiest seasons. In midsummer, crews often start early and avoid walls in full afternoon sun.

**Prep.** On older houses, scraping peeling paint, replacing soft boards, caulking and spot-priming can take longer than the painting itself. If two quotes are far apart, compare the prep each one includes before you compare the totals. Our [national guide to exterior painting costs](/blog/cost-to-paint-house-exterior/) covers the other price factors in detail.

## Hiring a painter in Texas

Licensing for painting-only work is mostly a local matter in Texas, so ask your city or county building department what applies where you live. Whatever the rules, ask every painter for a certificate of liability insurance, and check that it is current.

If your house was built before 1978, the old paint may contain lead. Under EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, contractors who disturb that paint must be certified lead-safe and follow containment and cleanup steps. Ask to see the firm's certification before work starts, and expect it to add some cost.

Get at least two or three written quotes that list the same things: which surfaces, how many coats, which paint line, what prep and repairs, and who cleans up. A quote far below the range usually skips prep or uses fewer coats.

## How we worked out these prices

National data from Angi, reported by NerdWallet, puts exterior painting at $1.50 to $4 per square foot of living area. Angi says labor makes up 75% to 95% of a professional paint job. We took 80% as the labor share and adjusted that part by Texas's painter wage compared with the national median, using Bureau of Labor Statistics 2025 wage data:

**Texas rate = national rate × (0.2 + 0.8 × $21.86 ÷ $23.75) = national rate × 0.936**

Paint and supplies cost about the same everywhere, so only the labor part moves. Treat the results as a planning range, not a quote. Local demand, the season and each painter's overhead all shift real prices.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much does it cost to paint a 2,000 sq ft house in Texas?

About $2,800 to $7,500 for the outside, with most jobs in the middle of that range. In Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos expect more, about $2,862 to $7,631.

### Where in Texas is exterior painting most expensive?

Of the metro areas above, Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos has the highest painter wages at $22.38 an hour, and San Antonio-New Braunfels the lowest at $20.88. Prices follow wages because labor is most of the bill.

### When is the best time to paint a house in Texas?

Spring and fall are easiest. You need about 48 hours of dry weather after each coat, so a painter will schedule around rain and avoid walls in full summer sun.

### Do I need a licensed painter in Texas?

It depends on your city or county, so ask your local building department. Either way, ask for proof of liability insurance.
